title: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing
summary: From building sovereign infrastructure and autonomous trucks to quantum-GPU supercomputing, Nordic countries are embracing and accelerating technological development.
body_markdown:
The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent.


Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems.


The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application.


## **NVIDIA’s Investments in the Nordics**


Over the past year, NVIDIA has invested in the technology ecosystem in the Nordics, including Sweden’s leading startups


Lovable


and


Legora.


[Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements](https://blogs.nvidia.com/gtc-berlin-2026-news/)


Lovable


, a Stockholm-based startup, provides a software creation platform that enables anyone to build and run software using plain language. In collaboration with NVIDIA, Lovable is optimizing inference for open models and training its models using NVIDIA Dynamo software and Nemotron tools.


Legora


provides an agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review and drafting across complex matters.


## **Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub**


The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry.


The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are


Bitdeer,


CoreWeave


,


Crusoe


,


Hyperstack,


Nscale


,


Verda


and


Volta


.


In Sweden, a consortium anchored by


Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments,


with


SKF


as strategic partner, launched


[Sferical One](https://sferical.ai/newsroom/leading-swedish-companies-launch-sferical-one-shared-ai-supercomputer) — a shared supercomputer running on two


[NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/dgx-superpod/) with 16 racks of


[NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/dgx-gb300/) and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using


[NVIDIA Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment.


## **Nordic-Built Intelligence**


Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure.


[Spotify](https://engineering.atspotify.com/2026/10/advancing-generative-recommendation-inference-our-collaboration-with-nvidia-on-tensorrt-llm) , which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query.


[ABB Robotics](https://www.abb.com/global/en/news/137409/abb-robotics-and-nvidia-white-paper-defines-transformative-impact-of-physical-ai-on-manufacturing) developed RobotStudio HyperReality using


[NVIDIA Omniverse](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. By combining NVIDIA’s advanced simulation capabilities with ABB Robotics’ virtual controller, running the same firmware as its physical robots, the solution enables engineers to train, test and validate robots virtually, while using real-world data to continuously improve the digital model. According to ABB Robotics, the solution delivers up to 99% simulation accuracy and reduces commissioning time by up to 80%.


Finnish telecom company


[Elisa](https://nam11.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fyrityksille.elisa.fi%2Fideat%2Fmoontalk-airi-real-time-ai-assistance&data=05%7C02%7Cebeisswenger%40nvidia.com%7Ce4430ec4c92b4ed0c2d508df29bf8858%7C43083d15727340c1b7db39efd9ccc17a%7C0%7C0%7C639275574771855820%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=%2Bv8nQ8VMmNnfXQBVAQfHXnCS8ch%2B68zVKKfA8xo6wq0%3D&reserved=0) is launching a beta of Moontalk AIRI, a real-time enterprise agentic assistant that retrieves information, captures insights and documents decisions during meetings and calls. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron open models and distributed infrastructure, it uses company data and low-latency networking to deliver fast, context-aware responses.


## **Nordic Startups Scaling on NVIDIA**


Sweden’s startup ecosystem raised $2.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and is projected to reach $5 billion for the year. This next generation is building fast — and on open models.


[Stilta](https://stilta.com/news/stilta-nvidia-partnership) is reinventing how companies protect their inventions with intellectual property. The Stockholm-based startup is post-training NVIDIA Nemotron open models to scale patent analysis from a single patent to entire portfolios — work that was previously out of reach. Nemotron gives


Stilta


the language model accuracy for continuous portfolio monitoring at scale, across the thousands of patents that large industrial and technology companies hold.


[ConfidentialMind’s SampoTron](https://confidentialmind.com/blog/sampotron-adapting-queries-reusing-index) ,


built on NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed, delivers more than 20% improvement in cross-lingual retrieval accuracy across English, Finnish and Swedish.


[Agaton](https://www.agaton.ai/post/nvidia-nemotron) , a platform that analyzes customer conversations in real time, is using NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to speed up Revenue Mining solution on live sales calls. By routing knowledge retrieval to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Agaton can cut response latency to deliver fast responses that inform customers’ buying decisions.


[Klang](https://research.klang.ai/releases/pianissimo/) , a Swedish speech lab, fine-tuned the NVIDIA Parakeet v3 model to create Pianissimo — a Swedish transcription model that reduces errors by 75% while being 64x faster than the most accurate alternative. Built on over 50,000 hours of Swedish speech using the open source


[NVIDIA NeMo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/products/nemo/) framework, the model is freely available on Hugging Face.


[Embedl](https://embedl.com/news/embedl-and-space-cargo-unlimited-bring-ai-autonomy-to-the-space-edge) , founded in Gothenburg and a member of the


[NVIDIA Inception](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/startups/) program for cutting-edge startups, and Space Cargo Unlimited unveiled an onboard prototype that monitors protein crystallization, flags anomalies and recommends actions on a single NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, without continuous ground connectivity.


[Sweden AI Factory](https://www.ri.se/en/news/sweden-ai-factory-and-nvidia-collaborate-to-shape-the-future-of-swedish-ai) — one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories — announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises across industries, including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming.


## **Autonomous Machines on Nordic Roads and Factory Floors**


In Sweden, advanced computing is also powering vehicles on the road and machines in factories.


[Volvo Cars](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/volvo-cars-and-nvidia-expand-partnership-to-advance-safe-automated-driving) is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with[NVIDIA Hyperion](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/autonomous-vehicles/) , Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door.


Autonomous freight company


[Einride](https://www.einride.tech/press/3365322) is building its next-generation Einride Driver on


NVIDIA Hyperion


for autonomous freight trucks, using the


[NVIDIA Halos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-trust-center/halos/autonomous-vehicles/) safety system and


[NVIDIA Cosmos](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/cosmos/) open world models.


Meanwhile,


[Toyota Material Handling Europe](https://toyota-forklifts.eu/about-toyota/news-and-editorials/toyota-material-handling-europe-and-softserve-to-reduce-autonomous-solution-commissioning-time-by-50-percent-using-nvidia-physical-ai/) — the world’s leading forklift manufacturer — is bringing autonomous machines to factory floors. In a collaboration with NVIDIA and


SoftServe,


Toyota Material Handling Europe


is adopting a simulation-first approach to autonomous material handling, cutting autonomous solution deployment time by up to 50% across its global engineering, manufacturing and innovation teams.


[Norrsken Foundation](https://www.norrsken.org/houses/stockholm-ai-lab) and NVIDIA are opening the Stockholm AI Lab, a physical hub for AI-native founders working on global challenges, set to open in 2027.


## **Quantum Meets Accelerated Computing**


Finally, Swedish companies are advancing quantum research using NVIDIA’s quantum computing platform.


Stockholm-based


[FirstQFM](https://firstqfm.com/news/firstqfm-nvidia-gtc-2026) used NVIDIA accelerated computing to train a model that reduces the execution time of quantum processors by 33% without sacrificing performance. Validated on a


QuantWare


quantum processor unit, this model optimizes how the operations needed by quantum algorithms are turned into detailed hardware instructions, accounting for detailed updates on how the hardware is calibrated.


*Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s*[GTC Berlin keynote](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/gtc/keynote/) *on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST.*
